rule3_grants.rule: RI-3 grants are exactly as declared, metastore-wide, for every principal and not only the declared ones
rule3_grants.means: Scoped to the metastore on BOTH axes. B-31 widened the share search; B-33 widened the principal search. A grant held by a recipient this config does not manage was previously filtered out by a rule whose stated job is 'grants are exactly as declared' -- the omission made the rule's name false. Nothing unmanaged is removed: an EXTRA grant on a MANAGED recipient needs --prune-grants, and a grant on an unmanaged principal is reported only, because this config does not own that principal and two writers of one object is the hazard.

rule4_tokens.rule: RI-4 token count within the platform bound; configured lifetime within the documented year
rule4_tokens.documented_max_note: Asserting our number against a bound we did not measure. The measurement is a year long.

lifetime_is_a_birth_property.behaviour: expiration_time is set on CREATE and is NOT re-sent on UPDATE.
lifetime_is_a_birth_property.because: An applier that re-stamped the lifetime on every run would extend every credential by the full window each time it ran, which converts a time-bounded control into an unbounded one for any environment where the applier runs regularly. Idempotent configuration and a bounded credential lifetime pull in opposite directions here, and silently extending is the worse of the two failures because nothing looks wrong.
lifetime_is_a_birth_property.consequence: Lifetime drift is REPORTED per recipient (lifetime_verdict) and changed only under --renew-lifetime.

rows.lifetime_means: This recipient's token window is not the configured one. The applier sets expiration_time on CREATE and deliberately does not touch it on UPDATE, so the difference persists and is reported rather than corrected. Use --renew-lifetime to change it on purpose.

rule7_share_isolation.rule: §3.1 share isolation -- per-use-case recipients, by channel
rule7_share_isolation.conops_text: §3.1: "one recipient per consuming agency or use case".
rule7_share_isolation.d2d_evidence: docs/11 §11.7 B-29; the error names the OTHER recipient
rule7_share_isolation.means: Two TOKEN recipients coexist for one logical consumer, so §3.1's 'one recipient per consuming agency OR USE CASE' is satisfiable per use case on D2O and refused per use case on D2D. One sentence, two answers, and the CONOPS does not split it by channel.
rule7_share_isolation.conops_action: §3.1 needs splitting by channel. As written it is a single sentence that is true for D2O and false for D2D, which is the worst shape for a control statement: whoever implements the D2D half will read it, try it, and get an error naming an object they did not touch.

known_incomplete.statement: Two of the three recipients hold a token in ACTIVATION_PENDING -- the link exists and has not been exchanged, so no client can read yet. The third, psp7-demo-recipient, holds no token at all. No credential in this model is live.
known_incomplete.consequence: "A recipient holds a grant" and "a recipient can read" are different claims and only the first is currently true. Every provider-side verdict in evidence/recipient-model.json is compatible with nobody being able to read anything, which is exactly what RKI-1 means and why the verdict says PROVIDER_SIDE.

known_incomplete.scope: the perimeter's topology, as distinct from its mechanism
known_incomplete.statement: T-02's production shape is an allow-list holding the GATEWAY's egress address, so that a direct call from anywhere else is refused. On this machine the gateway runs beside the test client and both leave through the same NAT address, so an IP allow-list cannot tell "via the gateway" from "direct" here. The MECHANISM is testable -- admit, then refuse, the same read -- and the TOPOLOGY is not, at any number of phases.
known_incomplete.consequence: AC1's direct-call refusal rests on an infrastructure assumption the CONOPS never states: that the gateway egresses from an address the recipient allow-list can name, and that no consumer can reach the sharing endpoint from an address on it. On a single-host deployment that assumption is false, and a T-02 reporting a pass without separating the two halves would carry it silently into v1.6.
known_incomplete.measured_by: tests/t02_ip_access_list.py phase 1b -- with the list holding only the operator's address, a successful read THROUGH the gateway shows the two addresses are the same one.
known_incomplete.closes_when: NEVER_LOCALLY for the topology half. It closes in a deployment where the gateway's egress address differs from any consumer's, at which point T-02 should be rebuilt around the gateway's address rather than the operator's. The deliverable here is the CONOPS sentence, not the test.
known_incomplete.owner: E1 Task 1.6 (the finding); Platform Security (the assumption)
